events.title: When the Violin Speaks: Klezmer, Memory and Jewish Life
events.description: Klezmer, the traditional music of the Eastern European Jews, has played a remarkable role in the revival of Jewish and Yiddish culture, among people around the world. For a Jew who becomes estranged from religious practice, or does not believe in God, the synagogue can feel intimidating or even alienating. But hearing a klezmer band play can offer a different kind of encounter. One can simply listen--to the crying violin, the dancing clarinet, the rhythms and melodies that carry memories of shtetls, weddings, migration, loss, humor and survival. Klezmer has become a cultural bridge, reconnecting generations of Jews and introducing non-Jews to the richness, complexity and emotional world of Yiddish culture.

events.title: Unlocking the Presidential Puzzle(s) with Mara Faccio
events.description: The Purdue University Research Center in Economics invites you to our November economic policy luncheon. Please register to join us for: Unlocking the Presidential Puzzle(s) with Mara Faccio 11:30 a.m.-12:30 p.m. Eastern Wednesday, November 11, 2026 Rawls Hall, 3rd Floor Commons 100 S. Grant Street Purdue’s West Lafayette campus Since 1927, the U.S. stock market has done substantially better under Democratic presidents than under Republicans, with the difference in annual stock market returns between the two parties averaging around 10% per year. This well-documented pattern has been dubbed the "presidential puzzle." Annual GDP growth shows a similar partisan gap. Faccio confirms this pattern using recent data. Before 1927, however, she finds that the "puzzle" reverses. Using data going back as far as 1791, she shows that annual stock market returns were almost 6% higher per year under Republican (or conservative) presidents. Annual GDP growth was 1.7% higher. Having examined competing explanations, Faccio concludes that the two opposing "puzzles" share one common source: investor risk aversion at election time. Whichever party won the election when risk aversion was high enjoyed higher subsequent returns. Mara Faccio is the Daniels School’s Tom and Patty Hefner Chair in Finance. Her primary research interests are in international finance and corporate finance. She is one of the most highly cited finance scholars. The PURCE faculty affiliate was among Stanford University and Elsevier’s top 2% of most influential scientists in the world for 2025. Space is limited for PURCE luncheons, and registration is required. Please register by noon on Friday, November 6. We look forward to seeing you in Rawls Hall for a catered lunch, networking, and a Q&A with Faccio following her talk. Parking is available in the nearby Grant Street Parking Garage. Reach out to us with any questions at purce@purdue.edu and (765) 494-3782. Learn more about our research center at business.purdue.edu/centers/purce.

events.title: Klezmer Music Workshop
events.description: The Klezmer Tradition: History, Sound & Performance This hands-on workshop introduces students to the history, musical vocabulary, and performance traditions of klezmer, the instrumental music of Eastern European Jewish communities. We will explore how klezmer developed through encounters with Jewish, Romani, Ukrainian, Polish, and other musical traditions, and how the music changed as Jewish musicians immigrated to America. Students will learn some of the fundamental scales, modes, rhythms, ornamentation, and characteristic melodic patterns that give klezmer its distinctive sound. Through listening and playing examples, we will examine styles such as freylekhs, bulgar, doina, hora, and other traditional forms. The workshop will also consider klezmer as a living musical language that has been revived, reinvented, and performed by musicians around the world. Musicians and singers of all levels are welcome. The workshop will be accessible to beginners while providing challenges for more advanced participants. Those who play an instrument are encouraged to bring it. events.description: AAARCC Book Series Screening Precarity: Hindi Cinema and Neoliberal Crisis in Twenty-First Century India Refreshments provided. RSVP and reading the book prior to the events are not required to participate. If you need accommodation to participate in this event, please email aaarcc@purdue.edu. The Book Talk with Author is co-sponsored by Purdue Graduate Student Government. ﻿ Book Discussion Thursday, November 5, 2PM-3PM AAARCC (915 5th St) Learn about the history and theory of "precarity" from Chapter 1, including examples of how Bollywood films mediate the discussions of precarious public spheres in India. Free books provided for first 5 individuals who RSVP and attend the book discussion! aaarcc.short.gy/screenrsvp​ This book is open access for Boilermakers and can be downloaded for free from: aaarcc.short.gy/precarity Book Talk with Author Thursday, November 12, 12-1 PM AAARCC (915 5th St) and virtual Join Dr. Anwer for lunch and reflection about how her book examines a filmic rendition of precarity, and how Bollywood is "not just a site of representation, but as an economic-cultural vector in its own right." Cannot join in-person? Livestream available through Microsoft Teams: aaarcc.short.gy/screenonline​ About Book & Authors Megha Anwer is a Clinical Associate Professor in the Department of English and Assistant Vice Provost for Research & Scholar Development at John Martinson Honors College. Dr. Anwer's research centers on perspectives and theories from urban studies, critical race studies, feminist studies, postcolonial studies and violence studies in a global and transnational context. Anupama Arora is a Professor of English and Communication at the University of Massachusetts Dartmouth. This book explores the role that Hindi films play in how precarity is mediated by film and what that mediation reveals about both contemporary India and the social life of the movies. It examines 19 Bollywood films that constitute India’s precarious public sphere, characterized by a pervasive and profound sense of professional-personal insecurity experienced by the vast majority. Screening Precarity: Hindi Cinema and Neoliberal Crisis in Twenty-First Century India is an intervention in the politics of representation, particularly of how marginal identities are shaped, scripted and screened when neoliberalism and authoritarianism enmesh. It is also a cultural analysis of how the biggest film industry in the world is embedded in global media networks and marshals state power and star power, national histories and transnational fantasies, structural impossibilities and individual agency. ﻿Flyer: https://aaarcc.short.gy/screenflyer

events.title: 2026 SUPPLY CHAIN CONSULTING LECTURE SERIES
events.description: PURDUE STUDENTS ARE INVITED Students across Purdue majors and programs are warmly invited to attend any or all sessions. Join us to learn directly from industry professionals, ask questions, explore career paths, and connect classroom ideas with real-world supply chain and consulting practice. ABOUT THE SERIES The 2026 Supply Chain Consulting Lecture Series connects Purdue students with experienced supply chain executives, consultants, alumni, and industry professionals to explore how organizations solve complex supply chain and operations challenges in practice. The series is an integral part of SCOM 469 — Supply Chain and Operations Analytics Consulting, a 3-credit experiential learning course that transforms the classroom into a professional consulting environment. Student teams apply supply chain theory, data analytics, AI-enabled tools, and structured consulting methods to real-world business and industry challenges. THE THREE-PILLAR EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING MODEL Consulting & Industry Study Projects — Students learn by solving real business and industry problems through corporate-sponsored consulting engagements and advisor-guided industry studies.Mentoring Program — Experienced alumni and industry professionals coach student teams on problem solving, analytics, project management, executive storytelling, and professional development. Jeffrey R. Powers, retired IBM executive and Purdue alumnus, chairs the Industry Advisory Board.Industry Lecture Series — Practitioners bring current challenges, emerging technologies, leadership lessons, and real-world decision making directly into the classroom. SCOM 469 builds on Purdue’s university–industry partnerships and experiential projects with organizations including Wabash, Rolls-Royce, Corteva, Taste, and other corporate and industry partners. For Fall 2026, students will work through two experiential project pathways: the corporate project Taste Omnichannel Dining Service Optimization and the industry study Enhancing Pharmaceutical Supply-Chain Resilience. WHY ATTEND? Learn from experienced professionals — See how practitioners approach ambiguous, high-impact supply chain problems.Understand professional practice — Explore consulting, leadership, sourcing, planning, program management, and digital transformation in action.Connect analytics and AI to execution — See how data, analytics, and AI shape consulting strategy and day-to-day supply chain decisions.Connect classroom frameworks to real decisions — Examine constraints, cross-functional trade-offs, and the realities of implementation.Build your professional network — Meet Purdue alumni and experienced industry professionals while exploring supply chain career paths.All Purdue students are welcome. You do not need to be enrolled in SCOM 469 to participate. Attend the sessions that match your interests, come prepared to ask questions and share perspectives, and use the series as an opportunity to learn and build professional connections. FALL 2026 LECTURE SCHEDULE SEPTEMBER 3 — Consulting 101 Isaac Tipton — CEO, Prowire USA The opening session introduces the foundations of consulting and structured problem solving. Drawing on professional experience, the speakers will discuss how consultants approach ambiguous business problems, work with clients and teams, communicate insights, and translate analysis into actionable recommendations. SEPTEMBER 17 — Program Management in Supply Chain: From Plan to Execution Michelle Kozlowski — Senior Program Manager, Amazon Catherine “Cathy” Nash — Sales & Operations Execution Planner, Constellation Brands Strong strategies create value only when organizations can execute them. This session focuses on program management, planning, coordination, accountability, and execution—examining how supply chain professionals move from plans and priorities to operational results across people, processes, and functions. OCTOBER 1 — Trade-Off Management + Cross-Functional Procurement & Sourcing Decisions Amanda Tronchin — Finance & Strategy Consultant, Pinnacle Strategy Group Eduardo Da Silva-Witzke — Aftermarket Sourcing Analyst, Cummins Inc. Supply chain and procurement decisions frequently require balancing competing objectives across cost, service, risk, quality, capacity, and strategic priorities. This session explores how professionals structure trade-offs, collaborate across functions, and translate financial, operational, and strategic considerations into sourcing and procurement decisions. OCTOBER 15 — Leadership, Influence & the Human Side of Supply Chain Consulting Kriti Gupta — Director of Operations, Amazon Nilo Cedeno-Guadamud — Global Category Manager, Wabash Analytics alone rarely produces organizational change. This session explores the human side of supply chain leadership and consulting—including stakeholder influence, relationship building, communication, team leadership, negotiation, and the ability to move organizations from insight to action. OCTOBER 29 — AI in Supply Chain: From Consulting Strategy to Everyday Execution Vishal Madisetti — Associate, Emerging Platforms, KPMG US Brookelle Mathieson — Life Sciences Supply Chain Management Consultant, Accenture Possible contributor: Khushi Karmokar — Procurement Analyst, ThoughtSpot AI is changing both how consultants solve problems and how supply chain professionals perform everyday work. This session explores practical applications of AI, analytics, automation, and emerging technologies—from consulting strategy and transformation initiatives to operational decision support, procurement, and day-to-day execution. NOVEMBER 12 — Planning, Constraints & Supply Chain Systems Thinking Kyle Harshbarger — Supply Chain Engineer, Marathon Petroleum Lauren Heiss — Senior Technology Consultant, EY The final session brings together planning, constraints, technology, and systems thinking. The speakers will connect MRP/ERP concepts, bottlenecks, lessons from The Goal, and real-world planning challenges to the broader question of how supply chains operate as interconnected systems. The session will also explore supply chain career paths and how the strategic role of the supply chain function varies across industries. CONNECTING INDUSTRY AND THE CLASSROOM The Industry Lecture Series is not designed as a collection of stand-alone guest presentations. Each session is integrated with students’ consulting and industry-study work. Student teams are encouraged to bring questions from their projects into the classroom, apply lessons from speakers to their analyses, and reflect on how different professionals approach similar challenges across industries. Student ambassadors will also work directly with speakers before selected sessions to help prepare and contextualize the lectures, providing another opportunity to develop professional communication, stakeholder-management, and networking skills. events.title: A Decade of Collective Remembrance: An Art Exhibition Commemorating the Victims of the Philippine War on Drugs
events.description: We would like to invite you to the opening reception of the art exhibit "A Decade of Collective Remembrance: An Art Exhibition Commemorating the Victims of the Philippine War on Drugs" on November 13, from noon-2pm at The Alab (Schleman 300). There will be food at the reception. Please save the date, and we hope to see you there. The exhibit will run until November 30, with open hours from noon-2pm on weekdays (except during the Thanksgiving Break). About the exhibit: A Decade of Collective Remembrance commemorates the 10th anniversary of the declaration of the ‘war on drugs’ in the Philippines, under the presidency of Rodrigo Duterte. The war on drugs was facilitated and intensified by digital disinformation operations and populist politics that othered and targeted mostly the urban poor. During the campaign, extrajudicial killings (EJK) were carried out by paramilitaries and the police, resulting in an estimated 30,000 bloody deaths, according to human rights groups. The exhibit makes space for the mourning, resistance, and most importantly, journey of grief of surviving family members of the victims. It bridges discourse on power, extrajudicial killings, state-sanctioned impunity, police brutality, and social justice. It features artworks by Filipino creatives that humanize the EJK victims, depict the violence of the war on drugs, and narrate the grief of the families and loved ones of the EJK victims. Collectively, the artists call upon the public to uphold due process, accountability, and human dignity. While this exhibit is being held, Duterte is facing charges of crimes against humanity at International Criminal Court (ICC). This was achieved not in small part through Filipinos’ and the global community’s sustained calls for justice. The A Decade of Collective Remembrance series of exhibits began in the Philippines in August 2026, first installed at the University of the Philippines, then at Ateneo de Manila University, and now at Purdue University. Through the exhibit, The ALab invites the Purdue community to be in solidarity with Filipinos as they demand justice. Faculty and TAs interested in bringing students to see the exhibit outside the open hours mentioned above, please email dadadocot@purdue.edu or gaizel@purdue.edu.

events.title: AI Bytes - How Much Help Is Too Much? Finding AI’s Place in Teaching and Learning
events.description: When students can turn to AI for help with everything from brainstorming to completing an assignment, it raises an important question: How much help is too much? The answer may depend less on the AI tool itself and more on what we want students to learn. How Much Help Is Too Much? Finding AI’s Place in Teaching and Learning explores how instructors can make intentional decisions about AI’s role in the learning process while helping students understand what is expected of them. Through examples and perspectives from instructors and teaching and learning experts, we’ll consider how AI can support learning objectives without replacing the critical thinking, participation, practice, and productive struggle that help students learn. We’ll also discuss the importance of transparency and clear communication, including how instructors can establish expectations around AI use and help students understand when, how, and why it may be appropriate in their coursework. Rather than starting with whether AI should or shouldn’t be used, we’ll focus on the learning we want to happen and work backward from there. Where could AI meaningfully support that learning? Where might it interfere? And how can instructors communicate those distinctions so students understand both the expectations and the reasoning behind them? Whether you’re experimenting with AI in your courses, concerned about how students are already using it, or still deciding what role it should play, you’ll leave with ideas for making intentional decisions about AI in your teaching and communicating those decisions clearly to students. events.description: The Executive Forum is open to the public, as seating permits, and provides opportunities for the exchange of ideas and discussion of topics and issues facing business and management. Winston is the Senior Director of Global Ad Sales at Apple Ads, overseeing 700 people across 22 offices around the world responsible for driving advertising revenue across Apple Services including the App Store, Apple News and Stocks, MLS and F1 on Apple TV, Apple Maps, and Apple Podcasts. Before Apple and Drawbridge, Winston held positions at Quantcast, Yahoo!, NBC Universal, General Electric, and IGN.com. Winston holds an MBA with a focus in marketing from Purdue University as well as a Bachelor of Arts from the University of Puget Sound with a major in Psychology and a minor in Philosophy. events.description: The Executive Forum is open to the public, as seating permits, and provides opportunities for the exchange of ideas and discussion of topics and issues facing business and management. Jennifer Richter serves as the Vice President, Supply Chain for The Clorox Company's US Cleaning business unit. In this role, she leads the supply chain networks, operations, and talent that support some of the company’s most recognized household and professional cleaning brands. Her work sits at the intersection of strategies across business aspirations, suppliers, manufacturing, distribution, technology, innovation, and people leadership. The Clorox Company champions people to be well and thrive every single day. Founded in 1913 and headquartered in Oakland, California, Clorox is driven by consumer-centric innovation. From cleaning to food storage to natural personal care, the company is committed to delivering clearly superior experiences through its trusted brands including Brita®, Burt's Bees®, Clorox®, Fresh Step®, Glad®, Hidden Valley®, Kingsford®, Liquid-Plumr®, PineSol® and Purell® as well as international brands such as Chux®, Clorinda® and Poett®. With operations in about 25 countries and territories, Clorox products are sold in more than 100 countries, helping people around the world live happier, healthier lives. Having recently been named by Forbes as one of America’s Best Employers for Women 2026, Clorox is proud to be recognized for efforts and impact in areas such as corporate and social responsibility, leadership development, inclusion and diversity, and culture. Since joining The Clorox Company in 2000, Jennifer has held roles across Supply Chain Planning, Customer Service, Transportation Operations, Customer Logistics, and Manufacturing for multiple Clorox businesses. Jennifer is a passionate people leader who believes a leader’s most important responsibility is enabling others to succeed. She believes optimism is a force multiplier, principles matter more than rules, and that performance and engagement are strongest when people are able to apply their strengths. Within Supply Chain, she has implemented a leadership approach that is grounded in raising the bar while creating the clarity, confidence, and space teammates need to do their best work. With the core leadership principle of “everyone wants to succeed” in mind, she is dedicated to developing talent, implementing inclusive leadership, supply chain competency building, and career pathing for her team. Jennifer graduated from North Carolina State University with BS degrees in Chemical Engineering and Pulp & Paper Science. She lives in Atlanta, GA with her husband and two children. A local community advocate, she serves on the board of directors for the Chastain Park Conservancy, an organization dedicated to restoring, enhancing, maintaining and preserving Atlanta’s second largest public park. She also enjoys creating lifetime memories with her family and volunteering with her local faith-based organization.
